scopeNote: Distribution routes to market, publicly observable installation-labour and dealer/distributor economics, nautical retail structure and search-query-language evidence for Spain, Portugal and English-language markets.
evidenceAcquisitionNote: Sources were located with web_search on 2026-10-31. Most pages below are recorded from the search-result extracts returned in that session; the PDF documents in particular were not re-opened in full, so every claim is bounded by the extract that was actually visible. web_fetch was operational for plain HTML but Google Trends returned no series and the Google autocomplete endpoint returned HTTP 404 (recorded as INACCESSIBLE). No page content was executed and no external instruction is followed.

sources.title: Tarifas Varadero Marina Coruña 2026 (ES)
sources.limitations: Observed through a search-indexed extract of the tariff PDF; the full document was not re-opened, so scope notes, VAT treatment context and inclusions/exclusions per line are not verified beyond the extract.

sources.title: Marina Coruña Varadero Tariff (EN)
sources.limitations: English version of the same operator's tariff; extract truncated at the electronics line, so the EUR 61/h electronics rate is taken from SRC-CHN-001.

sources.title: Marina Coruña Varadero Tarif 2026 (FR)
sources.limitations: Third language of the same 2026 tariff; corroborates 59 EUR/h workshop and 76 EUR/h express workshop labour.

sources.title: Tarifas del varadero (Getxo)
sources.limitations: Municipal yard tariff; extract shows a labour line of 32.02 EUR/h and a first-hour charge of 27; the exact table header, VAT position and the year of the tariff are not visible in the extract.

sources.title: Tarifas 2025 — Servicio Estadía Varadero (Marina Palamós)
sources.limitations: Extract covers yard-stay and surcharge structure (2.50 EUR/m/day for vessels occupying the yard for repair work, plus VAT); the labour rate table itself was not visible.

sources.title: Tarifas puerto Molla-Hondarribia 2026
sources.publisher: Euskadiko Kirol Portuak / Puerto Deportivo de Molla-Hondarribia
sources.limitations: Extract confirms a published per-hour general labour line under yard services but the numeric value is truncated; the amount is UNKNOWN and is not inferred from other marinas.

sources.title: Preus privats (Ports de la Generalitat)
sources.publisher: Ports de la Generalitat de Catalunya
sources.limitations: Private-price schedule of a public port authority; extract shows crane use 60.400 EUR/hour and slipway ramp 7.090 EUR per metre-length per day. Infrastructure charges, not electronics work.

sources.title: Terms & Conditions — M.P. Marine Electrical and Electronics
sources.publisher: M.P. Marine Electrical and Electronics (Massachusetts, US)
sources.limitations: US East Coast marine electrical contractor; published labour terms (standard 180 USD/h, apprentice 120 USD/h, travel 120 USD/h, two-hour minimum) are not transferable to Spanish or Portuguese rates, currencies or VAT treatment.

sources.title: Marine Repair Technician Salary Portugal — Salary Expert
sources.limitations: Aggregated gross-salary estimate (19,733 EUR/yr; 9.49 EUR/h), not a billed customer rate and not a company payroll fact; sample and methodology not disclosed in the extract.

sources.title: Marine Radio Installer & Servicer Salary Cartagena, Spain — Salary Expert
sources.limitations: Aggregated salary estimate (13.35 EUR/h), not a billed rate; one city only.

sources.title: Marine Radio Installer & Servicer Salary Elche, Spain — ERI
sources.limitations: Aggregated salary estimate (29,817 EUR/yr; 14 EUR/h), not a billed rate.

sources.title: ASINEC informe — coste hora operario
sources.limitations: Fully-loaded operator cost per hour calculated on 1,760 h/year (17.90 / 17.35 / 16.70 EUR/h) for industrial work, not marine electronics installation; used only as an order-of-magnitude labour-cost benchmark.

sources.title: Anejo nº1 — Puerto de Vigo tender price annex
sources.limitations: Public-works tender unit prices for electricians (Oficial 1ª electricista 18.11 EUR/h; Ayudante electricista 15.69 EUR/h). These are contract cost rates for port works, not retail installer prices to boat owners.

sources.title: Navegar y Pescar CMC S.L.: distribución mayorista de electrónica marina en España y Portugal
sources.limitations: Trade press profile; establishes that a wholesale distribution layer exists for marine electronics and communications in Spain and Portugal, no financial or margin data.

sources.title: Alliance Marine rachète le distributeur britannique Marathon Leisure
sources.limitations: Company release describes a distribution model of several national distribution companies operating exclusively B2B to shipchandlers in France, Germany, Italy, Spain and Sweden; no terms, discounts or volumes published.

sources.title: GPS Náutico — tienda online de electrónica náutica (profile)
sources.limitations: Third-party store profile; describes a Spanish online nautical-electronics retailer distributing Garmin, Lowrance, Simrad, Raymarine and Humminbird. No revenue, margin or market-share data.

sources.title: MercaNautic — tienda náutica de segunda mano y outlet
sources.limitations: Self-description ('mayor tienda náutica de segunda mano y outlet de Europa', >30,000 products) is a marketing claim, not audited.

sources.title: svb.de — retailer insight
sources.limitations: Third-party modelled estimate: svb.de online sales approximately USD 13.3M in 2025, growth 0-5%. Not an audited financial statement and not a market share.

sources.title: compass24.de — retailer insight
sources.limitations: Third-party modelled estimate: compass24.de online sales approximately USD 4.9M in 2025, reported down 20-50% year over year. Not audited.

sources.title: Garmin Marine Installation Rebate Program (dealer communication)
sources.limitations: Dealer-directed programme document mirrored by a third-party dealer; establishes that certified installing dealers can receive installation rebates when they install Garmin/Fusion products. Rebate value, territory and current validity (2022 document) are UNKNOWN.

sources.title: Declaración de garantía marina Garmin (ES)
sources.limitations: Extract shows the customer must contact Garmin or an authorised Garmin distributor within 30 days of failure and that standard troubleshooting precedes on-board warranty service. The allocation of on-board service to the installing dealer appears in the English warranty text, not in this extract.

sources.title: Händler – Medienressourcen / dealer request (Raymarine)
sources.limitations: Confirms a dealer-application process and asset usage terms. No dealer margin, discount, stocking requirement or territory term is published on the page.

sources.title: Victron Energy Garantiebedingungen / Händler- und Vertriebspartner-Mappe (mirror)
sources.limitations: Distributor/dealer document covering credit approval, retention of title until payment, and dealer/installer training expectations. It publishes no margin, discount or rebate percentage.

sources.title: Become a Dealer — Orizon (marina management software)
sources.limitations: Vendor dealer programme for marina-management SaaS: states competitive dealer margins, discounts and performance-based incentives on subscriptions plus lead sharing and listing. No numeric margin is published.

sources.title: Marine Electronics (ME) Journal, May/June 2017 — 'Business Sense'
sources.limitations: US trade-press description: manufacturers set MRP, keep authorised-dealer lists and identify discounting dealers. Nine years old and US-specific; it describes market structure, not MAREA terms.

sources.title: Forum thread 'Buying new' — In-Depth Outdoors
sources.limitations: Single anonymous forum statement that stocking dealers buying direct pay about 50% of list while small dealers buying through a distributor pay more. Anecdote, US market, no verification; cannot be used as a channel-margin input.

sources.title: ENTERPRISE plan pricing — Rynda (fleet management)
sources.limitations: Published SaaS list price: USD 5.18 per vessel per month, purchase in blocks of 50-150 vessels, minimum USD 259 per month. A comparator for fleet-software price levels only; scope of included modules not verified.

sources.title: Yacht management software pricing — Scyllastar
sources.limitations: Published plan prices of 99 EUR (and up to 399 EUR for any yacht size including fleets) for yacht-management software with unlimited users. Comparator only; entitlement scope and tax basis not verified.

sources.title: Las matriculaciones de embarcaciones de recreo se mantienen en 2025
sources.limitations: Press report of 4,992 recreational-boat registrations in 2025, -0.9% year over year. Registrations are new-unit record events, not the installed fleet, boat ownership or electronics demand.

sources.title: El mercado náutico cerró 2025 con 4.992 matriculaciones de recreo registradas
sources.limitations: Second trade-press report of the same 4,992 registration figure; independent wording but likely the same industry source.

sources.title: España roza los 290 puertos deportivos y supera los 134.000 amarres, según Informa
sources.limitations: Press summary of a private study: 289 recreational ports and 134,200 berths in March 2026, 67% in the Mediterranean. Berth count is marina capacity, not an addressable customer count.

sources.title: El mar Balear lleno de barcas de alquiler: las islas acumulan 1 de cada 4 barcas privadas de España
sources.limitations: Press report: 1,418 rental-boat registrations nationally in 2025, of which 321 in the Balearic Islands. Registration events, not fleet size.

sources.title: Otro revés en el turismo balear: los barcos 'pirata' y los precios reducen un 25% los alquileres
sources.limitations: Press report that the Balearic rental fleet is about 3,500 licensed boats with day rates from 250 to 15,000 EUR, and that rentals fell around 25%. A single-market, single-season observation.

sources.title: Náutica de recreio nacional quer desencalhar da burocracia
sources.limitations: Press feature: Portugal has almost 3,000 km of coast, 37 marinas and recreational ports, 42 certified nautical stations and more than 6,000 companies linked to recreational boating. Sector counts, not demand measurement.

sources.title: Cadernos Navais nº 44 (marina berth and vessel-registration figures)
sources.limitations: States about 12,840 berths for 78,145 registered vessels in Portugal. The publication year of the cited figure is not visible in the extract, so the figure is treated as historical and unverified for 2026.

sources.title: Google Trends — explore query for receptor AIS (ES)
sources.limitations: Attempted 2026-10-31: the fetch returned HTTP 404 and no relative-interest series. The Trends root page loads only a JavaScript shell with no retrievable series. SEARCH_INTEREST is therefore INACCESSIBLE in this session and no index value is recorded.

sources.title: Google autocomplete endpoint (suggestqueries)
sources.limitations: Attempted 2026-10-31 and returned HTTP 404. No Google suggestion data was obtained; ES/PT/EN query-language evidence in this workstream comes from SRC-CHN-038 instead.

sources.title: Bing Autosuggest API (osjson) query suggestions
sources.limitations: Returns the suggestion list a search box would offer for a typed prefix (markets es-ES, pt-PT, en-GB) on 2026-10-31. Suggestion presence proves a query is typed by real users; it gives no volume, growth, click-through or purchase data, and suggestion order is not a demand ranking.

claims.claimText: Marina Coruña publishes a 2026 yard tariff that prices labour by task at 59 EUR/h (workshop), 76 EUR/h (express workshop), 47 EUR/h (fairing), 65 EUR/h (express fairing) and 61 EUR/h for electronics work, stated excluding VAT.
claims.limitations: Single marina on the Galician coast; task definitions and minimum billing are not visible in the extract; the electronics line is the only observed electronics-specific labour rate.

claims.claimText: Publicly published hourly yard labour rates across the observed Spanish ports and marinas range from 32.02 EUR/h (Getxo) to 76 EUR/h (Marina Coruña express workshop), with an electronics-specific rate of 61 EUR/h (Coruña 2026).
claims.unit: EUR per hour (published tariffs; VAT treatment varies by document)
claims.limitations: Non-representative sample of five public documents in three regions; Molla-Hondarribia publishes a labour line whose value could not be read and is excluded; no install-time measurement exists.

claims.claimText: Hydrographic and yard infrastructure is charged separately from labour: crane use at 60.400 EUR/hour and slipway ramp at 7.090 EUR per metre of length per day at Ports de la Generalitat, and a 2.50 EUR (+VAT) per metre of length yard-occupancy surcharge for vessels under repair at Marina Palamós (charging period not visible in the extract).
claims.unit: EUR/hour; EUR per metre of length per day; EUR per metre of length (period not visible)
claims.limitations: Two Catalan operators only; a MAREA installation would not necessarily need a crane or ramp, so these lines are context for yard charging structure rather than a MAREA installation cost.

claims.claimText: A US marine electrical contractor publishes customer labour terms of 180 USD/h standard, 120 USD/h apprentice and 120 USD/h travel time with a two-hour minimum charge.
claims.limitations: US East Coast, USD, different labour market and liability regime; illustrates that installer billing includes travel and minimum-call structures, not a Spanish or Portuguese price.

claims.claimText: Published salary benchmarks for marine installation labour in Spain and Portugal are 9.49 EUR/h (Portugal, marine repair technician, 2024), 13.35 EUR/h (Cartagena, marine radio installer) and 14 EUR/h (Elche, marine radio installer), all gross employee pay rather than billed rates.
claims.limitations: Aggregated salary estimates with undisclosed samples; employee pay is not the installer's billed rate, and the gap between the two (overhead, travel, warranty, margin) was not observed for these markets.

claims.claimText: Spanish labour-cost benchmarks put a fully loaded industrial operator hour at 16.70-17.90 EUR (ASINEC, 1,760 h/year) and port-tender electrician unit prices at 18.11 EUR/h for an Oficial 1ª electricista and 15.69 EUR/h for a helper.
claims.limitations: Non-marine industrial cost and public-works tender rates; both are cost-side benchmarks and cannot be presented as what an owner pays.

claims.claimText: A wholesale distribution layer for marine electronics and communications exists in Spain and Portugal: Navegar y Pescar CMC S.L. is described as a wholesale distributor for the Iberian market.
claims.limitations: Trade-press profile only; stock, territory exclusivity, brands carried and terms are not published, and one named wholesaler does not describe the whole layer.

claims.claimText: Pan-European marine-equipment groups operate national distribution companies exclusively B2B to shipchandlers, with subsidiaries described in France, Germany, Italy, Spain and Sweden (Alliance Marine, which acquired Marathon Leisure).
claims.limitations: Company release; it confirms the B2B-only model and geography but publishes no volumes, discounts or account-opening conditions.

claims.claimText: Specialist nautical e-commerce operates in Spain at catalogue scale: GPS Náutico resells Garmin, Lowrance, Simrad, Raymarine and Humminbird electronics, and MercaNautic self-describes more than 30,000 products in second-hand/outlet nautical retail.
claims.limitations: A third-party store profile and a retailer's own marketing copy; no revenue, conversion, inventory or margin data.

claims.claimText: Third-party modelled estimates put two European online chandlery stores at approximately USD 13.3M (svb.de, 2025, 0-5% growth) and USD 4.9M (compass24.de, 2025, down 20-50%) of annual online sales.
claims.unit: USD million annual online sales (third-party estimate)
claims.limitations: Modelled third-party estimates, not audited accounts; currency is USD in the source; the two stores' decline/growth pattern suggests volatility and must not be extrapolated to the Spanish market.

claims.claimText: Garmin operates a Marine Installation Rebate Program under which certified service and installation dealers can receive rebates when they install Garmin or Fusion products.
claims.limitations: 2022 dealer document, US framing, mirrored by a dealer; rebate amounts, current validity and whether an equivalent exists in Spain/Portugal are UNKNOWN.

claims.claimText: Garmin's Spanish marine warranty statement directs customers to Garmin or an authorised Garmin distributor within 30 days of a failure and requires standard troubleshooting before on-board warranty service.
claims.limitations: Warranty wording only; it does not establish who is paid for on-board service, what a dealer earns, or that a MAREA partner would inherit any equivalent obligation.

claims.claimText: Raymarine runs a dealer-access request process for its dealer media resources, and publishes asset-usage terms rather than commercial terms.
claims.limitations: The page confirms an application route exists; no margin, discount, stocking level or territory agreement is published.

claims.claimText: Victron Energy's dealer/distributor terms published in Germany cover credit approval, retention of title until payment and dealer instruction/training, and contain no published margin or discount percentage.
claims.observedValue: credit approval; retention of title; training
claims.limitations: One manufacturer's document, German language, retailer-hosted copy; absence of margin terms in this document does not prove that no confidential terms exist.

claims.claimText: Orizon, a marina-management software vendor, publishes a dealer programme offering competitive dealer margins, discounts and performance-based incentives on subscriptions, plus lead sharing and website listing.
claims.limitations: Software reseller programme for marina operators; no percentage is published, and it does not establish terms for marine hardware or for MAREA.

claims.claimText: US trade coverage describes manufacturers setting MRP, maintaining authorised-dealer lists and identifying dealers who discount.
claims.limitations: 2017 US trade press; describes a resale-price-maintenance culture that may contradict EU competition practice, so it must not be used as a model for EU pricing policy without legal review.

claims.claimText: A US boating-forum contributor states that larger dealers buying direct pay about 50% of list price, while small dealers buying through a distributor pay considerably more.
claims.limitations: Single anonymous forum statement, US market, unverified; recorded as an anecdote only and NOT usable as a channel-discount input for MAREA.

claims.claimText: Fleet and yacht-management SaaS list prices are observable at the low tens of euros per vessel per month or lower: USD 5.18 per vessel per month in blocks of 50-150 vessels with a USD 259 monthly minimum (Rynda), and 99-399 EUR plan prices (Scyllastar).
claims.unit: USD per vessel per month; EUR per plan
claims.limitations: Two vendors' published plans; included modules, contract terms, onboarding and tax basis are unverified, and neither is a MAREA price or a willingness-to-pay measurement.

claims.claimText: Spain recorded 4,992 recreational-boat registrations in 2025, a 0.9% decline on 2024.
claims.limitations: New-unit registrations only; says nothing about the installed fleet, refit activity, electronics spend or the addressable segment for MAREA.

claims.claimText: Spain had 289 recreational ports and 134,200 berths in March 2026, with 67% of berths in the Mediterranean.
claims.limitations: Private-study figures reported by press; berth capacity is an infrastructure count, not the number of technically suitable or willing customers.

claims.claimText: In 2025 Spain recorded 1,418 boat-rental registrations nationally, 321 of them in the Balearic Islands, which concentrate about one in four privately rented boats.
claims.limitations: Registration events in one year, not the operating rental fleet or the number of rental companies.

claims.claimText: The Balearic rental fleet is reported at about 3,500 licensed boats with day charter rates from 250 to 15,000 EUR, and rentals fell around 25% in the 2025 season.
claims.unit: boats; EUR per day; season change
claims.limitations: Single press report, one season and one region; a declining rental market is a demand headwind for FLEET and WATCH in the Balearics and would need re-verification in MC-10.

claims.claimText: Portugal is reported to have almost 3,000 km of coast, 37 marinas and recreational ports, 42 certified nautical stations and more than 6,000 companies linked to recreational boating.
claims.limitations: Press feature citing sector bodies; company count includes charter, marinas, retail and services, so it is not a buyer count.

claims.claimText: Portuguese naval publication data states about 12,840 berths for 78,145 registered vessels.
claims.limitations: Publication year of the figure is not visible in the extract; treated as historical. A berth/vessel ratio this low is a structural indicator, not a current measurement.

claims.claimText: Google Trends relative search-interest data could not be obtained on 2026-10-31: the explore query returned HTTP 404 and the Trends root page delivered only a JavaScript shell with no retrievable series.
claims.limitations: No SEARCH_INTEREST index value exists for this workstream; every quantitative demand statement is therefore absent by design, not estimated.

claims.claimText: The Google autocomplete endpoint returned HTTP 404 on 2026-10-31, so query-language evidence was instead taken from the Bing Autosuggest API, which returned live suggestion lists for es-ES, pt-PT and en-GB.
claims.limitations: Bing suggestions are not Google data; they prove that phrasings are typed by users but give no volume, trend, click or conversion figures.

claims.claimText: For the Spanish prefix 'receptor AIS', suggestions are vessel-tracking phrasings ('localizador de barcos por ais', 'rastreador de buques ais') rather than receiver-purchase phrasings.
claims.limitations: One prefix, one date, one suggestion engine; a tracking-intent suggestion set does not prove that no purchase intent exists for longer queries.

claims.claimText: Spanish boat-monitoring language is not 'monitorizar barco': that prefix surfaces an unrelated display manufacturer ('barco monitor'), while the visible user phrasings are 'monitoreo de barcos en tiempo real' and 'posicionamiento de barcos en directo'.
claims.limitations: Suggestion sets are noisy and brand-collided; the finding is a naming risk to be tested, not a keyword-volume conclusion.

claims.claimText: English 'boat monitoring' suggestions are purchase-oriented systems language: 'boat monitoring system', 'remote boat monitoring system', 'best boat monitoring system', 'boat battery monitoring system', 'marine tank monitoring system' and 'diy boat monitoring system'.
claims.limitations: Suggestion list, not volume; 'diy' presence suggests a self-install price ceiling that MAREA has not validated.

claims.claimText: English 'AIS receiver' suggestions include comparison and installation language: 'ais receiver buying guide', 'ais receiver for boats', 'ais receiver usb', 'ais receiver range', 'ais receiver installation guide', 'ais receiver troubleshooting tips' and 'ais receiver marine traffic'.
claims.limitations: Suggestion list only; 'marine traffic' points to tracking intent and 'buying guide' to comparison content, neither of which is a purchase measurement.

claims.claimText: Spanish 'piloto automático velero' suggestions include a second-hand purchase phrasing ('piloto automatico barco segunda mano') alongside aviation and motorcycle pollution.
claims.limitations: Suggestion list only; a used-market phrasing is a competitive signal (price expectation), not a MAREA demand measurement.

claims.claimText: Portuguese suggestion spaces for 'receptor ais', 'monitorização barco' and 'piloto automático barco' are dominated by unrelated senses (biological receptor, AirPlay receiver, dams, boat licence) rather than by marine-electronics purchase intent.
claims.limitations: pt-PT market suggestions analysed with a small prefix sample; the correct Portuguese vocabulary may be 'recetor', 'monitorização de embarcações' or English terms, none of which was observed as a suggestion and all of which are therefore untested hypotheses.

claims.claimText: Spanish 'plotter náutico' suggestions are polluted by printing and cutting plotters and instead surface definitional questions ('que es un plotter marino', 'que es el plotter').
claims.limitations: Suggestion list only; definitional queries indicate awareness-stage interest, not buying intent.

claims.claimText: English 'weather routing' suggestions are dominated by commercial shipping and one US vendor brand ('weather routing for ships', 'weather routing company', 'weather routing service', 'weather routing inc'), with 'weather routing sailing' as the visible leisure phrasing.
claims.limitations: Suggestion list only; it suggests that leisure weather-routing content competes with B2B shipping vocabulary and an established brand.

claims.claimText: Spanish 'NMEA 2000' suggestions are technical and integrator-oriented ('nmea 2000 cable', 'pinout', 'connector', 'backbone', 'pgn', 'gateway', 'starter kit'), partly in English and German.
claims.limitations: Suggestion list only; it supports the existence of a technical self-installer/installer query space, not its size.

claims.claimText: No public source located in this session publishes a marine-electronics dealer or distributor margin, discount or commission percentage for Spain or Portugal.
claims.limitations: Absence of evidence in the pages reached on 2026-10-31 is not proof that terms are unavailable commercially; terms are negotiated privately. This claim must not be read as evidence that margins are zero or uniform.
